source: India Meteorological Department (IMD) Marine Weather Division

signals_definitions.Signal 1: Cautionary — Squally weather with surface wind 40-50 km/h likely.
signals_definitions.Signal 2: Warning — A depression has formed, wind speed 50-60 km/h.
signals_definitions.Signal 3: Danger — Port threatened by squally weather, wind 60-70 km/h.
signals_definitions.Signal 4: Danger — Severe cyclonic storm, wind 70-90 km/h expected.
signals_definitions.Signal 5: Danger — Storm likely to cross coast keeping port to the left.
signals_definitions.Signal 6: Danger — Storm likely to cross coast keeping port to the right.
signals_definitions.Signal 7: Danger — Storm likely to cross over or near the port.
signals_definitions.Signal 8: Great Danger — Severe cyclone likely to cross keeping port to left, winds >100 km/h.
signals_definitions.Signal 9: Great Danger — Severe cyclone likely to cross keeping port to right.
signals_definitions.Signal 10: Great Danger — Super cyclonic storm crossing directly over port.
signals_definitions.Signal 11: Communication Failure — Radio/radar contact lost with meteorological observatory.
